text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - British stocks rallied Friday on continued speculation about takeovers and strength on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 index jumped 68.8 points, or 1.5 percent, to 4,645.0, for a gain of 23.7 from last Friday.
FRANKFURT - German shares rose as well, with the 30-share DAX adding 22.26 points to 3,695.29. The index added 147.45 for the week.

PARIS - Ignoring political uncertainty, French shares closed higher for the sixth straight session, helped by a strong Wall Street performance. The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 1.06 percent, a gain of 28.40 points to 2,719.25, for a gain of 135.31 from last week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares kept this week's record-setting pace, posting a fourth straight record close on the back of a strong U.S. dollar and strength in the financial sector. The All share SPI jumped 40.54 points to 3,368.53, and was up 172.97 for the week.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended little changed as investors were cautious ahead of U.S. payroll data. The 225-share Nikkei average fell 2.40 points to 20,485.75, but was up 416.94 from last Friday.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks fell ahead of a long weekend despite Hongkong Telecom's record-setting jump, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index tumbled 140.39 points to 14,655.13, and was off 102.68 for the week.
SYDNEY - Australian stocks ended lower but managed to stay above the 2,600 mark. The All Ordinaries Index came off its lows to end off 3.3 points at 2,600.9, for a drop of 9.6 points on the week.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold stocks broke out of a slump as precious metals prices moved higher. The all-share index rose 43.7 points to 7,262.2, a gain of 240.5 for the week, the industrial index edged up 6.8 to 8,476.7 for a rise of 236.5 from last Friday, and the gold index jumped 35.3 points, or 3.1 percent, to 1,175.6. Its gain was 1.8 points for the week.
